## Abstract
The GEO series GSE309890, associated with BioProject PRJNA1363958, examines resistance emergence in *Escherichia coli* under the influence of antidepressant sertraline. The dataset includes six samples, processed on Illumina HiSeq 4000 platforms. Raw sequencing reads for these samples are publicly available under SRA, with six runs providing RNA-Seq data. Assembly workflows can be applied to these raw reads.

## I. Introduction
**Background.** GEO series GSE309890 focuses on the metabolic and genomic factors influencing antibiotic resistance in *Escherichia coli* under stress induced by sertraline.
**Literature Review.** No PubMed article is linked to this study. The dataset investigates critical molecular traits tied to resistance and offers RNA-Seq data for deep exploration.
**Knowledge Gap.** The ability to study *E. coli's* resistance mechanisms with raw reads remains crucial for understanding intervention mechanisms through genome assembly.
**Objective & Hypothesis.** To validate if raw reads are accessible and compatible with assembly workflows for downstream analyses.

## II. Materials and Methods
**Study Design.** The BioProject accession (PRJNA1363958) was resolved to gather raw sequencing read links and associated metadata from SRA.
**Materials.** Databases: GEO and SRA.
**Procedures.**
1. Resolved GSE309890 to its associated BioProject (PRJNA1363958).
2. Using resolved BioProject ID, retrieved all associated SRA run data to collect raw reads.
3. Analyzed platform compatibility for assembly processing (Illumina HiSeq 4000).
**Statistical Analysis.** Reviewed six runs covering GSM-based samples (RNA-Seq).

## III. Results
**Data Presentation.**
| Run Accession | Sample Name | Total Bases | Avg. Length | Size (MB) | Platform | Download Link |
|---------------|-------------|-------------|-------------|-----------|----------|----------------|
| SRR36018645   | GSM9284457  | 3,486,517,800 | 300         | 917       | HiSeq 4000 | [Link](https://sra-downloadb.be-md.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sos10/sra-pub-zq-1002/SRR036/36018/SRR36018645/SRR36018645.lite.1) |
| SRR36018644   | GSM9284458  | 3,124,630,200 | 300         | 801       | HiSeq 4000 | [Link](https://sra-downloadb.be-md.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sos10/sra-pub-zq-1002/SRR036/36018/SRR36018644/SRR36018644.lite.1) |
| SRR36018643   | GSM9284459  | 3,516,065,700 | 300         | 926       | HiSeq 4000 | [Link](https://sra-downloadb.be-md.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sos10/sra-pub-zq-1002/SRR036/36018/SRR36018643/SRR36018643.lite.1) |
| SRR36018642   | GSM9284460  | 3,597,738,300 | 300         | 955       | HiSeq 4000 | [Link](https://sra-downloadb.be-md.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sos10/sra-pub-zq-1002/SRR036/36018/SRR36018642/SRR36018642.lite.1) |
| SRR36018641   | GSM9284461  | 3,599,154,600 | 300         | 948       | HiSeq 4000 | [Link](https://sra-downloadb.be-md.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sos10/sra-pub-zq-1002/SRR036/36018/SRR36018641/SRR36018641.lite.1) |
| SRR36018640   | GSM9284462  | 3,408,998,700 | 300         | 894       | HiSeq 4000 | [Link](https://sra-downloadb.be-md.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sos10/sra-pub-zq-1002/SRR036/36018/SRR36018640/SRR36018640.lite.1) |

**Findings.** Six RNA-Seq paired-end runs from *E. coli* were successfully retrieved. Illumina HiSeq 4000 sequencing ensures data quality suitable for genome assembly workflows.

## IV. Discussion
**Interpretation.** The raw reads from GSE309890 can be downloaded and are compatible with genome assembly workflows, given their paired-end layout and platform specifications.
**Context.** The study enables insight into resistance traits, inviting deeper analysis of key genetic components.
**Limitations.** Further optimization or filtering may be needed to ensure integrity during the assembly process.
**Conclusion & Future Directions.** Data availability provides an opportunity to explore assembly workflows targeting resistance pathways. Exploring additional replicates or specialized software can enhance biological inference.

[1] [GEO Series GSE309890 details](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE309890)  
[2] [SRA Data for PRJNA1363958](https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/esearch.fcgi?term=PRJNA1363958&retmax=10)  

## Acknowledgments
Data providers: GEO and SRA via NCBI E-Utilities.
